labelled_by: Hand-labelled ground truth for the eval harness. Quotes are verbatim substrings of the transcripts.

pain_points.label: Over-ordering leads to costly food waste

quotes.quote: I'd guess we throw away 10 to 15 percent of what we buy in a slow week.
Last quarter we threw away about 2,400 euros of vegetables and pork across both sites.
If I only need half of that, I still have to buy 150 euros, so I buy extra and hope.
For the smaller location that's more than a week's worth, so some of it goes to waste.
Gut feeling and last week's numbers on a notepad.

pain_points.label: Daily stock-taking is too much effort

quotes.quote: After a 12-hour service the last thing I want is to count tomatoes on my phone.

H1.why: R-01 and R-03 report significant waste; R-02 reports under 3 percent. Only 3 interviews.

H2.why: All three reject daily manual inventory tracking; R-03 tried and abandoned an app.

H3.why: R-01 and R-03 both name supplier minimums as a cause of over-buying; R-02 has no minimums. Small sample: 3 interviews.

stances_note: Per-interview stance on each hypothesis with verbatim quotes. Interviews not listed did not discuss it.

supporting: I'd guess we throw away 10 to 15 percent of what we buy in a slow week.

contradicting: I'd say waste is under 3 percent.

contradicting: After a 12-hour service the last thing I want is to count tomatoes on my phone.
An app would be one more thing to update, and my staff wouldn't keep it up.

H1.question: What did you throw away at the end of last week?
H1.purpose: Get a concrete, recent measure of waste.
H1.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.

H1.question: How do you know how much food you waste in a month?
H1.purpose: Find out whether they measure waste at all.
H1.bias_check: Neutral; does not assume waste is significant.
follow_ups: When did you last look at that number?

H3.question: Tell me about your last order from a supplier with a minimum.
H3.purpose: Test whether minimums actually cause over-buying.
H3.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.

PP4.question: Walk me through what happens in the kitchen after the last service of the night.
PP4.purpose: See whether there is any room for stock-taking in the real routine.
PP4.bias_check: Asks for the routine without mentioning an app.

PP3.question: How did you decide the quantities in your most recent order?
PP3.purpose: Understand how ordering decisions are made today.
PP3.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.
follow_ups: What information did you look at?

PP1.question: Tell me about the last time you had too much of something in stock.
PP1.bias_check: Asks about a specific past event, so the answer is a fact, not a prediction.
follow_ups: What did you do with it?
